absent: Host Spectre state sources and mitigation policy behind workaround queries.
SMCCC argument and result accessor mechanics, exception syndrome and trap length helpers, and secure monitor taxonomy.
Filter configuration lifecycle including insertion, removal, concurrency and persistence of entries.
Provisioning of firmware bitmaps, timer offsets, stolen time base addresses and system suspend enable flag.
PSCI version selection for a virtual machine and affinity validation plus mask derivation details.
Power primitives for wait, power off, wake, reset handling and inter CPU request delivery.
Guest memory write path, locking and error handling for stolen time initialization.
Randomness source properties, UUID values and bitmap helper semantics.
Userspace hypercall and system event protocols beyond exit structure population.
Vendor UUID value and reserved vendor feature range management.

findings.text: Guest SMCCC trap handler shared by the virtualization layer. It reads the trapped function identifier for the calling virtual CPU, resolves a filter decision, serves version and architecture feature queries plus paravirtual time, vendor identity and time synchronization requests locally, delegates randomness requests to a dedicated helper, and sends every other identifier to PSCI handling. Completion distinguishes guest resume with results already installed from a required exit to userspace.

Guest PSCI dispatcher. It first applies an allow check that can reject the call outright, then chooses an implementation based on the guest visible PSCI version across the legacy and modern families. Unknown versions are reported as unsupported rather than dispatched.

Guest randomness dispatcher for the standardized randomness family. It answers version and capability queries, returns multi word identity, and forwards fixed width random requests to a sized generator. All other outcomes report lack of support.

Paravirtual stolen time interface. A features query reports usability of the registration calls only after the shared area has been enabled. An initialization entry records a scheduling baseline, clears the guest visible area through a locked guest write, and returns the guest address of that area or an invalid sentinel when disabled.

Handled versus exit completion contract. Handlers that install results into guest registers request immediate guest resume. Handlers that populate the run exit area request suspension with control transferred to userspace. System power transitions use the exit path and preload a failure result so an accidental resume does not observe success.

Filter precedence for SMCCC. An explicitly configured filter decision other than handle wins immediately. Only when the filter says handle do firmware bitmap membership and the built in default allow set get consulted, with denial as the final outcome.

Built in default allow set independent of firmware bitmaps. Version and architecture feature queries are always served. Power state calls in the low standard range and the small legacy KVM range are also served by default.

Firmware bitmap gating per family. Randomness calls consult a standard bitmap bit, paravirtual time calls consult a standard hypervisor bitmap bit, vendor identity queries consult a vendor feature bit, and vendor time synchronization consults a separate vendor bit. Identifiers outside these families do not match any bitmap.

Filter table lookup behavior. When no filter has been configured every call is treated as handle. When configured the table is indexed by the numeric function identifier and a missing entry is treated as handle, so only present entries can deny or forward.

Version and architecture feature handling. A version query reports a fixed modern revision. An architecture features query examines its first argument and maps three workaround selectors to host mitigation states where vulnerable keeps the deny default, mitigated reports success, and unaffected reports a distinct unaffected or not required result, with one workaround suppressing firmware reporting when a CPU feature indicates system wide protection. A time features selector reports success only when the corresponding hypervisor bitmap bit is set.

Remaining SMCCC dispatch. Paravirtual features go through a dedicated query, stolen time registration returns its guest address on success, vendor identity expands a UUID across four result words, vendor features return two bitmap words with a documented reserved middle range, time synchronization fills results through a helper, randomness delegates to its own dispatcher, and anything else falls through to PSCI.

Precision time handling. Host realtime and counter values are captured together and accepted only when the active clock source is the architected counter. The guest selects virtual or physical reference through its first argument with distinct offsets subtracted, and unknown selectors keep the deny default. Valid time and cycle values are each split into high and low halves across four result words, relying on the top time bit staying clear for realistic dates.

PSCI version dispatch. After the allow check the handler selects minor specific modern behavior for four minor revisions, legacy handling for two older revisions, and a deny with a one time warning for anything else. Minor selection affects which newer power extensions are advertised and honored.

Legacy power handling. Version reports a fixed older revision, suspend is emulated as a wait, power off stops the caller, power on and affinity info normalize 32 bit callers before sharing wider logic, migration type reports a multiprocessor trusted OS value, and system shutdown or reset generate system events while preloading failure and requesting an exit.

Modern feature advertisement. A features query first reuses the allow check on its argument, then reports support for the legacy set plus version and self description, gates system suspend on an enable flag, gates system reset extension on minor revision, and for the newest shutdown extension returns a hibernate capability value instead of plain success.

Modern power extensions and oldest legacy. System suspend requires its enable flag and exits to userspace without altering guest registers so userspace can read the original arguments. System reset extension requires a minimum minor and an architected or vendor type range. Newest shutdown extension requires its minor and strict argument values. The oldest legacy version supports only power off and power on.

Virtual CPU power on. The caller supplies a target identifier plus entry address and initial argument. The target must pass affinity validation, resolve to an existing virtual CPU, and be observed stopped under its power lock, otherwise callers see already on or invalid parameters depending on version. On success the target receives entry state including caller endianness, a pending reset is requested, ordering is enforced before publishing runnable state, and the target is woken.

Affinity information query. The caller supplies a target affinity and a lowest level. Both are validated and a mask derived from the level selects the significant affinity bits. All virtual CPUs whose masked affinity matches are examined, reporting on if any match is running, invalid when nothing matches, and off otherwise.
Suspend emulated as wait for interrupt. Standby and power down requests are treated identically and register state is preserved. Completion always reports success with wake driven by interrupts.

System event generation. Shutdown, reset and their extended variants stop every virtual CPU under per CPU power locks, request sleep across the virtual machine, and populate a system event with type, count, flags and an exit reason. Suspend instead only populates a suspend event without stopping CPUs.

Stolen time enablement. Features and registration are reported usable only when the per virtual CPU base address differs from the invalid sentinel. Enabling snapshots the current scheduling delay as a baseline, writes zeroed initial values to the guest, and returns the base address for the guest to use.

Randomness generation. Version reports a fixed revision and features report success only for the five known selectors. Identity returns four words derived from a UUID. Random requests specify a bit count that must not exceed three times the width, are fulfilled from host randomness across machine words, have surplus high bits cleared, are packed differently for narrow and wide widths, and use a temporary buffer that is explicitly cleared after use.

Power on serialization. The target power lock is held while testing stopped state, programming pending reset state, requesting reset, publishing runnable state and waking. A write barrier orders reset programming before the runnable publication so observers of runnable also observe the reset.

System shutdown serialization. Generation of shutdown and reset events iterates every virtual CPU, takes each power lock in turn to publish stopped state, releases it, and only then issues a global sleep request, preventing further guest execution before userspace reinitializes.

Firmware feature container. The virtual machine holds separate bitmap words for standard features, standard hypervisor features, vendor hypervisor features and an additional vendor word. Individual bits gate randomness, paravirtual time, vendor identity and time synchronization families.

Per virtual CPU power, time and reset state. Reset state carries an entry address, endianness flag, initial argument and pending indicator. Power state pairs a lock with a runnable or stopped value. Stolen time pairs a guest base address with a last delay baseline. Timer state carries separate virtual and physical counter offsets subtracted for guest reads.

Userspace exit payloads. A hypercall exit carries the trapped function number plus flags distinguishing secure monitor calls and narrow trap length, with a hypercall exit reason. A system event exit carries a zeroed structure filled with event type, data count, flag word and a system event exit reason.

SMCCC request lifecycle. A trap resolves to deny, handle or forward. Deny installs a not supported result and resumes. Handle serves locally or through delegated PSCI and randomness dispatchers with their own completion. Forward populates a hypercall exit and suspends. Unknown filter outcomes are treated as deny with a diagnostic.

Virtual CPU power lifecycle. A stopped CPU becomes runnable through power on with pending reset. A runnable CPU becomes stopped through power off or through a system shutdown or reset event. Suspend leaves the CPU runnable in a wait. System suspend leaves power states unchanged while still exiting.

PSCI version layering. Modern handling serves its own version, features and extended power calls and delegates all other selectors to legacy handling. Legacy handling serves the historic power set. The oldest version is isolated to two calls and never reaches newer logic.
Unexpected filter outcome is diagnosed with a rate limited warning and converted to denial with a not supported result, avoiding unhandled behavior if configuration yields an unknown action value.
Unknown guest visible PSCI version triggers a one time warning and a not supported result, preventing dispatch on an unrecognized version.

Width safety. A 64 bit marked power call from a 32 bit guest mode is rejected as unsupported. The 32 bit forms of power on, affinity info, system suspend and newer power extensions first narrow upper arguments before entering the shared wider path.
No resume after shutdown. Shutdown, reset and extended shutdown preload an internal failure result and request an exit. If userspace mistakenly resumes, the guest observes failure instead of success.

Data hygiene for time and randomness. Randomness rejects excessive bit counts, clears unused high bits and explicitly clears its temporary words. Time synchronization leaves the deny default untouched when the clock source or selector is unsuitable and depends on realistic time values keeping a high bit clear.

SMCCC application interface. Distinct function families exist for version, architecture features, paravirtual time features and registration, vendor identity and features, vendor time synchronization and five randomness selectors. Result codes distinguish not supported, success, not required and unaffected outcomes, and the version query reports a fixed modern revision.

PSCI application interface. Guest visible versions span oldest legacy, older legacy and modern minor revisions with a constructed version value. Return codes distinguish success, not supported, invalid parameters, already on and internal failure. Affinity levels distinguish on and off, migration type reports multiprocessor behavior, and reset and shutdown extensions define warm, vendor and hibernate types with strict argument checks.

Power and exit interface values. Power states distinguish runnable and stopped with reset and sleep requests coordinating transitions. Exit reasons distinguish hypercall and system event. Hypercall flags distinguish secure monitor origin and narrow trap length. System event types distinguish shutdown, reset and suspend with additional flags marking extended reset and shutdown forms.

Paravirtual, randomness and time constants. An invalid guest address sentinel marks disabled stolen time. Randomness defines a fixed version, success, not supported and invalid parameter results plus narrow and wide widths with a three times width bit limit. Time synchronization defines virtual and physical counter selectors and requires the architected counter identifier.
